title.value: APOE alleles are associated with sex-specific structural differences in brain regions affected in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia
title.justification: The title of the paper is clearly mentioned in the header and in the citation provided.
title.quote: Savignac C, Villeneuve S, Badhwar A, Saltoun K, Shafighi K, Zajner C, et al. (2022) APOE alleles are associated with sex-specific structural differences in brain regions affected in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia. PLoS Biol 20(12): e3001863. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3001863

analysis.description: This paper examines the relationship between APOE alleles and structural differences in brain regions associated with Alzheimer's disease, using data from the UK Biobank. It explores sex-specific effects and integrates genetic and environmental risk factors.

type.justification: The paper involves practical analysis using a dataset of approximately 40,000 participants and performs a variety of statistical techniques to analyze data.
type.quote: By leveraging the power of the approximately 40,000 participants of the UK Biobank cohort, we assessed impacts from the protective APOE ε2 and the deleterious APOE ε4 Alzheimer’s disease alleles on these structural relationships.

name.justification: The study focuses on the structural variations in brain regions and genetic influences, which are central topics in neuroscience.
name.quote: Alzheimer’s disease is marked by intracellular tau aggregates in the medial temporal lobe (MTL) and extracellular amyloid aggregates in the default network (DN). Here, we examined codependent structural variations between the MTL’s most vulnerable structure, the hippo- campus (HC), and the DN at subregion resolution in individuals with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia (ADRD).

name.justification: The paper examines the impact of genetic variations, specifically APOE alleles, on brain structure and associated Alzheimer's disease risk.
name.quote: We assessed impacts from the protective APOE ε2 and the deleterious APOE ε4 Alzheimer’s disease alleles on these structural relationships.

name.justification: The use of the UK Biobank cohort and the exploration of phenotypic profiles categorize this paper within the field of epidemiology.
name.quote: Analyses of the rich phenotypic profiles in the UK Biobank cohort further revealed male-specific HC-DN associations with air pollution and female-specific associations with cardiovascular traits.

name.justification: The paper primarily utilizes the UK Biobank dataset for its analyses.
name.quote: By leveraging the power of the approximately 40,000 participants of the UK Biobank cohort, we assessed impacts from the protective APOE ε2 and the deleterious APOE ε4 Alzheimer’s disease alleles on these structural relationships.
